solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aggressive tough guy clubhouse put behind bar

indicators.note: putting one thing behind another fixes the order: the first-named item goes second

parts.note: but as a preposition means except, the same as bar
CH is a dictionary abbreviation for clubhouse

explanation.surface: A violent heavy is thrown out of the clubhouse bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put behind' is the order instruction: the clubhouse abbreviation goes after the word for bar, giving BUTCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch describes a person, often a heavy, who is aggressively and toughly masculine.

clue.text: British king riding wild yak, very shaggy?

indicators.note: a wild animal is untamed, so the letters of the beast's name run loose into a new order

parts.note: standard abbreviation for British
R for rex, Latin for king
the animal's name, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A British monarch rides a shaggy wild yak.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAKY means overgrown with brake, i.e. bracken; the question mark admits that 'very shaggy' is a playful gloss on land thick with fern.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is braky is dense with bracken and thicket, so it looks rough and shaggy.

clue.text: Knight Commander, Lieut. or Corp.? Quite wrong

indicators.note: if the letters are quite wrong as they stand, they must be put into a different, correct order

parts.note: every letter of the two ranks and the word between them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a knight commander is a lieutenant or a corporal, and is told that is quite wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The ranks look like the point of the question, but they are only a supply of eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The turcopolier was the knight of the Hospitallers who commanded their light cavalry, the turcopoles.

clue.text: Scottish spice? Silly person forgetting name

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a clown is a fool
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A cook asks about a Scottish spice and calls themselves silly for forgetting its name.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOWN loses its N to leave CLOW, the Scots form of clove.
explanation.definitionFit: Clow is the Scots dialect word for the clove, the dried flower bud used as a spice.

clue.text: Part of calendar that's hot, sun in central spot after rising

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so the letters run backwards
one thing set in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the nave is the central hub of a wheel
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A calendar entry is hot and has the sun at the centre of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The nave here is the hub of a wheel, not the body of a church. Hesvan, also spelt Heshvan, is a month of the Jewish calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesvan is the second month of the Jewish civil year, so it is one part of that calendar.

clue.text: Privileges keeping camp in step

indicators.note: something keeping another holds it inside itself

parts.note: a pas is a step in dancing
a tent is what you camp in

explanation.surface: Special privileges let a group keep their camp in step with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS holds TENT: PA(TENT)S. 'in step' looks like a phrase, but 'in' only links and 'step' is the dance term pas.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters patent grant special rights, so patents are official grants of privilege.

clue.text: American Indian as old man accompanied by wife

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, i.e. as
pa is an informal word for father
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A Native American figure is described as an old man with his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The Quapaw are a Native American people originally of the Arkansas region, so a Quapaw is an American Indian.

clue.text: Like a disputatious philosopher, quite bold when clashing, I see

indicators.note: things clashing knock against one another and get jumbled up

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
I and see, read as the letter C

explanation.surface: A philosopher fond of argument turns quite bold whenever views clash, so the speaker notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' sounds like a reply, but it is I followed by the letter C. A quodlibet was a scholastic debating question.
explanation.definitionFit: Quodlibetic means given to subtle scholastic argument, which is the hallmark of a disputatious philosopher.

clue.text: Number featured in a record throughout

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears within it

parts.note: A plus LOG, a written record
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A song features on a record all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a song on the record; it is only N, put into A LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'all along', the word means for the whole time, from start to finish.

clue.text: Liberal theologian benefited on lifting hearts in past (simple)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the aorist is the simple past tense of Greek grammar

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts
if something paid, it benefited you

explanation.surface: A liberal theologian once gained from raising people's hearts in simpler times.
explanation.walkthrough: H and PAID read upward give DIAPH, which goes into AORIST. An adiaphorist held that some doctrines and rites were matters of indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Adiaphorists were tolerant Protestant theologians who treated non-essential rites as indifferent, a liberal stance.

clue.text: Climber requiring salt eaten into by sun and air

indicators.note: what is eaten into has something else bored inside it

parts.note: Attic salt is wit, so salt means wit
S is the abbreviation for sun
an air is a tune, as is an aria

explanation.surface: A climbing plant needs salt in the soil, plus plenty of sun and air.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt is the sharp wit of 'Attic salt', not the mineral the gardening surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria (wisteria) is a twining woody vine, a classic climbing plant on walls.

clue.text: Sexual allure and pungency, part of Thailand's currency

parts.note: SA stands for sex appeal
a tang is a sharp taste or smell

explanation.surface: Sex appeal and a sharp tang feature in Thailand's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The satang is a hundredth of a baht, the subsidiary coin in the Thai monetary system.

clue.text: Rubber absent in thickening ribbons

indicators.note: the first items go inside the following word

parts.note: a roux is a flour-and-fat base that thickens sauces
ule is a Central American rubber tree
A is the abbreviation for absent

explanation.surface: With no rubber to hand, some ribbons thicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' suggests an eraser or tyre; it is the ule, a Central American tree yielding rubber, and its letters go after the first two of the sauce base.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a narrow piped roll of fabric used as trimming, so rouleaux are rolled ribbons.

clue.text: 'Lady I converted' — as Paul said of me in Philippi?

definitions.text: 'Lady I converted' — as Paul said of me in Philippi?

indicators.note: something converted is changed in form, so these letters change their order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman quotes Paul describing her as the lady he converted at Philippi.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts 16, Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, was converted by Paul at Philippi; the whole clue is both the anagram and her description.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is the woman Paul baptised at Philippi, the first recorded European convert, so she fits the clue's speaker.

clue.text: A log, roots crumbling with pith — one that's good on grass?

indicators.note: something crumbling breaks into bits that can re-form in another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
the pith of a matter is its gist

explanation.surface: A rotting log with crumbling roots and pith lies in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good on grass' sounds like a tennis player; it means an expert in grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: An agrostologist is a botanist who studies grasses, so they are knowledgeable about grass.

clue.text: Lunch involved in number one card game

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the next item
something involved is tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of lunch, rearranged
number one is a child's word for urinating

explanation.surface: A lunch features a top-class card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' looks like the best; it is the nursery word for a wee, PEE, with the jumbled LUNCH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Penuchle (pinochle) is a card game for two to four players using a double pack.

clue.text: Lovely place cheers sloths etc

parts.note: Eden is paradise
ta-ta is a goodbye, as cheers is in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone toasts a lovely spot full of sloths and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'cheers' is also a casual goodbye, so it gives TA-TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the old zoological order of toothless mammals including sloths, anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: Official's assistant chaps leaving one ME state for another

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so those letters drop out

parts.note: Yemen is a Middle Eastern country
chaps are men
Oman is another Middle Eastern state

explanation.surface: An assistant's chaps move from one Maine state to another.
explanation.walkthrough: ME looks like Maine, but it is Middle East: YEMEN loses MEN and OMAN replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman can be a subordinate officer or attendant who assists an official, as in yeoman of the guard.

clue.text: Sort of stripper? The lady's after identity being given a lift

indicators.note: after fixes the order, sending the lady's word to the end
in a down clue, lifted letters read upward, i.e. backwards

parts.note: your self is your identity
her, the lady's

explanation.surface: A woman stripper is lifted up after her identity is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a dancer: a flesher removes flesh from hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A flesher is a worker who strips flesh off hides, or a Scots word for a butcher.

clue.text: Bridge partners, past making interference

indicators.note: to interfere is to come between, so one item slips in between the others

parts.note: South and North are partners at bridge
pa. is the dictionary abbreviation for past

explanation.surface: At bridge a partnership of old is spoiled by interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game, given 'partners'; it is the definition, a span.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the arch or stretch of a bridge between supports, and can mean the bridge itself.

clue.text: Some passed out after upending port

indicators.note: upending a thing turns it upside down, so in a down clue the letters read the other way
some of the phrase means only a part of its letters

parts.note: a run of letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Some people passed out after drinking port bottoms up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink; it is the Black Sea port.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa (Odesa) is a major seaport on the Black Sea coast of Ukraine.

clue.text: One's related to another number, almost a contradiction

indicators.note: almost all means one short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an antilogy is a self-contradiction

explanation.surface: Saying one number relates to another is almost a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTILOGY without its last letter gives ANTILOG, short for antilogarithm.
explanation.definitionFit: An antilog is the number whose logarithm is a given number, so each is tied to another number.

clue.text: Single services will do them, aces catching edge of court

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an ace is a one, so aces are oners

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its outermost letter, here the start

parts.note: the first letter of court

explanation.surface: Single services suit players who serve aces at the edge of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture hides churchgoing: oncers attend only one service on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncers are people who go to church once each Sunday, so a single service suits them.

clue.text: Couples cheat, becoming linked with you and me

indicators.note: linked words interlock like chain links, so their letters thread through each other in a new order

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
us covers you and me

explanation.surface: Cheating couples get mixed up with the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short words interlock like chain links, their letters alternating one from each.
explanation.definitionFit: Duos are pairs, especially of performers, so couples is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fish rising on Tees? Only one of them for initiate

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the pope is another name for the ruffe, a small freshwater fish

indicators.note: only one of several identical items is wanted, so just a single letter

parts.note: Tees spelt out is the plural of the letter T

explanation.surface: A fish rises in the River Tees, but only one of them will do for a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees looks like the northern English river; it is the letter T, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: An epopt was someone initiated into the highest grade of the Eleusinian mysteries.

clue.text: Do this to net and what's often crude follows!

definitions.text: Do this to net and what's often crude follows!

indicators.note: an instruction to work on the next word, here read as reworking its letter order

parts.note: the three letters to rearrange
crude oil is the familiar phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about a net, with crude oil to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: To entoil is to catch in toils, a net, so the whole clue both builds the word and hints at its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Entoil means to ensnare or entangle, as if trapping something in a net.

clue.text: Abandoned miss from part of east Mediterranean (ban lifted)

indicators.note: a ban lifted is removed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: of Lebanon, a country at the eastern end of the Mediterranean
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman cast off by someone from the eastern Mediterranean finds a ban lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned miss' looks like a jilted girl; it means an obsolete verb for to miss, LEESE, an old form of lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Leese is an archaic and Spenserian word for to lose, so it is a disused word for miss.

clue.text: Cuts out extracts in church office, retiring

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a see is a bishop's office or seat
clips are short extracts from a film

explanation.surface: A retiring church official cuts out extracts from the parish records.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or overshadow, so it cuts out light or attention.

clue.text: The Scots are alarmed and run away with English invading

indicators.note: an invader goes into territory, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: to fly is to flee
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The Scots take fright and flee as the English invade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a border war, but 'The Scots' just flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fley is Scots for to frighten, or to be afraid, so in Scotland the alarmed fley.

clue.text: Scuppered the fine Polish man-of-war (13, four words)

indicators.note: a scuppered plan is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: A fine Polish warship has been scuttled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is just fodder, and scuppered nicely hints at sinking ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship of the line was a large sailing warship fit for the line of battle, a man-of-war.

clue.text: Wayne maybe takes strip off back to rest?

indicators.note: back means turning round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to peel is to strip the skin off

explanation.surface: A performer named Wayne strips off before resting.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Sleep is a British ballet dancer, so 'Wayne maybe' is one hint; 'rest' gives the plain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep is the surname of dancer Wayne Sleep, and to sleep is to take one's rest.

clue.text: Pause in verse to strive against, mostly after end

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to die is to come to an end
resist means to strive against

explanation.surface: A poet pauses in a line, resisting nearly to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' is a verb here, to die, not the close of the line the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a dieresis is the break where the end of a word coincides with the end of a metrical foot.

clue.text: Indian staple in our community, like Kama Sutra?

indicators.note: one item goes inside the other

parts.note: EC, the European Community, which Britain then belonged to
roti is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: An Indian staple has found a place in Britain, like the Kama Sutra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian theme of roti and Kama Sutra carries the surface; EC is the old European Community.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is an ancient Indian text on sexual love, so it is famously erotic in character.

clue.text: Time, that old reaper, we hear

definitions.note: an old word, as 'that old' hints

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: Father Time carries a scythe, his reaping blade

explanation.surface: Father Time, that old reaper, is talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Sythe is an old spelling of sith or sithe, meaning time or occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic English a sythe or sithe was a time, as in 'many sithes', an occasion.
